answer: Agents can gate valuable actions on a proof-of-personhood credential issued after an in-person check, then let each credential authorize only one active account. A newcomer might earn reputation by completing a small task, like tagging ocean data or writing a sonnet, but the credential still sets the limit. An attacker can create many software identities cheaply, yet must recruit and verify a separate real person for each one, adding coordination, payment, and exposure costs; a jetty of fake accounts alone earns no extra influence.
